walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Presentation & Interpretation — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Presentation & Interpretation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Presentation & Interpretation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is most affected by extreme outliers?
options: mean
median
mode
range

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).
Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
Limits always equal zero unless the function is constant.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.

11/12 — find a common denominator: 8/12 + 3/12.

2/12, by multiplying instead of adding.

mcqs.q: Does the limit of f(x) as x approaches a have to equal f(a)?
options: The limit is always just the value of f at that point — that's how you compute it.
No — the limit can exist even if f(a) is undefined or different from the limit.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
Limits always equal zero unless the function is constant.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Box plots”?
options: Show min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Visualise spread, skew, outliers. Useful for comparing distributions.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cumulative frequency”?
options: Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sampling”?
options: Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.

sequence.def: Collect raw data from a population sample — the first step.
Summarise the centre of the data with averages.
Measure how spread out the data is.
Flag extreme values using the spread measures.
Running totals up each class — used to read quartiles.
Drawn from quartiles to display spread visually — final summary.
